Reviewer: m3 pool job review-4475, Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), mkinney seat (`.claude-team2`); did not write or refresh this PR.

**Needs changes before merge.** This is the first review of this PR. It lists each finding of the whole diff. There is one blocker. The cause of the blocker is newer main, not the code of this PR.

Tier: SAFETY. The PR adds a new geometry module. Its hole coordinates go into posted G-code. I ran three mutations myself (see below). No recorded program moves.

## What looks good

- The recipes are in `camcraft-geometry` (`hole_pattern.rs`). The MCP tool in `app` only reads JSON and runs commands. The crate placement obeys "`app` holds the document".
- No new crate dependency. No `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `scripts/`, `.github/` or process file changes.
- Each recipe refuses non-finite numbers, a count of 0, a pitch or diameter of 0 or less, and more than 10,000 holes, by the field name. The grid product uses `checked_mul`. I found no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests.
- The two `CreateOperation` commands are built and checked before either runs. One undo removes both operations. The pin tests undo and redo.
- The stock-height swap (`top_of_model` to `top_of_stock`) fixes the "no model loaded" refusal at generate. A height in `params` still wins.
- Provenance lines are present. The decision record `docs/decisions/3195-hole-patterns.md` is complete. The new test files join the existing `geo2d` and `mcp` directory suites. The body has `Changelog:`, `Goldens moved: None` and `Fixes #3195`.

## Results (local, host m3, macOS, trial merge with `upstream/main` 6898b02ea)

Trial merge `8f5ad012c` (HEAD^1 = `e152c869a`): clean, with no conflicts.

| `cargo xtask gate light` | not completed: the release build stalled for 60 min with no output, and the gate watchdog killed it. This is a host build stall, not a test result. It is not a pass. |

Not run by me: the other 970 or so steps of the full quick plan. A change in `geometry` makes the quick plan fall back to the batch plan. The author reports 1015 steps, 0 failed, on the PR head before the merge.

## Mutations (each one restored after the run)

- M4 from the body (no full-turn guard for a partial circle): `degenerate_and_non_finite_patterns_are_refused_by_name` is red. Confirmed.
- M2 from the body (the main operation is not built again after the spot drill): `a_bolt_circle_with_a_spot_drill_is_one_undo_step_and_posts_g81` is red at `hole_pattern.rs:69`. Confirmed.
- My own mutation (sign of the sine term in the bolt-circle `y`): `a_full_bolt_circle_...` and `a_partial_bolt_circle_...` are red. A wrong hole position does not pass.

## Requested before merge

1. **Blocker: `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is stale after the merge with main.** Class: a generated file that two PRs change, each of which adds a tool. After this PR branched, main added `edit_user_holder` (#4391). The merged file has 139 tool rows, but line 4 still says "The server lists 138 tools". Bare `upstream/main` is consistent (138 rows, "138 tools"). The PR head by itself is also consistent. Only the merge is red, so the PR causes this red step together with newer main.
   Fix: merge `upstream/main` into the branch. Then write the file again with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- mcp reference > docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`. Then run `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_doc_drift`. One rule closes the class: always generate this file again after each merge of main, and never edit it by hand.

## Optional, non-blocking (suggested follow-ups, P7)

- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:362`, called from `hole_pattern_tools.rs:258`: `clearance_warning` writes `out["warning"]`. It replaces the off-stock warning that line 255 sets. If both apply, the agent does not see the off-stock holes. Join the two sentences with "; " instead.
- `crates/geometry/src/hole_pattern.rs:100`: the doc says that `points()` refuses "two holes on the same place". Only the point list has this check. A line, grid or circle with a very small pitch or diameter (for example a 1e-9 mm diameter circle) puts all its holes on one place. Either check coincidence for each recipe (one rule over the output points), or correct the doc.
- `crates/geometry/src/hole_pattern.rs:85` (`clean`): `v * 1e9` overflows to infinity for |v| > about 1.8e299, and a very large finite pitch times the index can also overflow. Such input is refused later (a non-finite value goes to JSON `null`, and the patch does not read), but the message does not name the field. I found this by reading the code and did not test it. A finite check over the output points would give a refusal by name.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs:27-29`: the new `mod hole_pattern` lines sit under the `#3449` comment, which describes `op_type_fields`. Move them above the comment.
- The tool description does not say that `xy` is in world coordinates (`HoleDto` is world XY). For a setup whose WCS origin is not the world origin, an agent can type program coordinates and get holes at a shifted position. The off-stock warning helps only when the shift moves a hole off the stock. One sentence in the description would prevent this.

The PR keeps its ready flag (AGENTS.md: on red the reviewer sets `needs-rework` and keeps the ready flag). A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
